Focus areas

Territorial Intelligence and Technological Innovation

We apply data science, GIS, artificial intelligence, modeling, sensors, automation and technological innovation to accelerate sustainability and improve decision making.

This focus area develops territorial analysis projects, an open satellite observatory, and data and instrumentation capabilities for other projects.

Select a service to know its function, objective, restrictions and general mathematical formulation.

Design of measurement and instrumentation campaigns

Function: convert technical questions into variables, sensors, locations and frequencies.

Aim: obtain representative information with controlled uncertainty.

Restrictions: range, accuracy, calibration, power, communications, environment, access and cost.

Design of experiments and statistical validation

Function: convert a technical or scientific hypothesis into a reproducible experimental protocol by defining factors, levels, treatments, controls, replicates, response variables and an analysis strategy.

Aim: obtain statistically valid evidence using the lowest reasonable number of trials while controlling the main sources of variability.

Restrictions: randomization, replication, sample size, resource availability, instrumental precision, confounding variables, statistical assumptions, traceability and reproducibility.

Restrictions: physical laws, data, identifiability, scale, validation and propagation of uncertainty.

Aim: minimize deviations, consumption and failures.

Restrictions: stability, response times, actuator limits, safe stop and manual control.

Data analysis and responsible artificial intelligence

Function: detect patterns, estimate variables and support decisions.

Aim: minimize the validated error and provide a demonstrable improvement over base methods.

Restrictions: privacy, bias, explainability, representativeness, security and human supervision.
